cards.headline: Body of suspect found after double homicide at Vero Beach library
cards.body:
The body of a suspect who killed his wife and another man at a Vero Beach library before escaping into the ocean has been recovered, according to authorities. The suspect fled into the Atlantic Ocean following the double homicide at the library in Vero Beach.

The violent incident unfolded at a Vero Beach library facility, where two people were killed before the suspect made his escape. Authorities had been searching for the man after he entered the ocean waters off Vero Beach. The recovery of the body brings closure to the manhunt that began after the library shootings.

The two victims included the suspect's wife and another man who were both at the library at the time of the attack. Law enforcement officials responded to the scene at the Vero Beach library following reports of the shooting. The suspect's decision to flee into the ocean complicated the search efforts.

The investigation into the double homicide continues as authorities work to piece together the events that led to the deadly violence at the Vero Beach library. The recovery of the suspect's body from the ocean ends the immediate public safety threat, but questions remain about what precipitated the attack. cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman faces attempted murder charges after setting bedroom door on fire with victim inside
cards.teaser: A 26-year-old Port St. Lucie woman is charged with attempted murder and arson after allegedly setting fire to a bedroom door while a 62-year-old woman was trapped inside and then attacking her.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police arrested Michelle Picard, 26, after responding to reports of a domestic disturbance and active house fire at around 9:05 p.m. Sunday in the 1500 block of Southeast Airoso Boulevard. Officers arrived to find flames inside the residence and immediately worked to evacuate everyone safely.

According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, the 62-year-old victim first noticed smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door and discovered Picard standing nearby when she opened it. When the victim attempted to retrieve a fire extinguisher, Picard allegedly physically attacked her and tried to prevent her from putting out the fire. Police say Picard made threatening statements and attempted to push the victim toward the flames. The victim managed to escape to a bathroom, lock the door, and call 911. During the emergency call, Picard could be heard banging on the bathroom door in the background.

Officers found Picard outside the residence and detained her. She resisted arrest, causing injuries to one officer's leg and requiring another officer to receive medical treatment. Picard faces charges including attempted murder, arson, battery on a law enforcement officer, and resisting arrest with violence. The Port St. Lucie Police Department continues to investigate the incident.

The arrest follows an investigation that began with an initial complaint and has now expanded to include a second alleged victim. The school bus driver faces charges related to lewd and lascivious molestation involving students who were under the driver's supervision. Law enforcement officials confirmed that the second victim came forward after the initial arrest was made public.

The case has raised concerns among parents and school officials in St. Lucie County about student safety on school buses. The driver's employment status and the specific schools or bus routes involved have not been disclosed by authorities. The investigation remains active as law enforcement works to determine if there may be additional victims.

Parents in St. Lucie County are being urged to talk with their children about the case and to contact law enforcement if they have any information related to the investigation. The school district is expected to review its protocols for background checks and monitoring of bus drivers. The suspect faces multiple charges and is in custody awaiting further legal proceedings. cards.headline: Florida Sues OpenAI and CEO Sam Altman Over ChatGPT Safety Risks
cards.body:
Florida has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and its CEO Sam Altman, accusing the artificial intelligence company of hiding safety risks from ChatGPT users and prioritizing profits over public safety. The lawsuit claims OpenAI allowed ChatGPT to aid and abet mass shooters, according to multiple reports. The legal action represents one of the first major state enforcement efforts against AI companies over safety concerns.

The state alleges that OpenAI concealed known risks associated with ChatGPT from users while deploying the technology widely across Florida and the nation. According to the complaints, the company failed to implement adequate safeguards to prevent misuse of the AI chatbot in dangerous situations. The lawsuit specifically references incidents where ChatGPT allegedly provided assistance related to mass shooting scenarios, raising urgent questions about AI safety protocols and corporate accountability.

The legal action affects millions of Floridians who use ChatGPT for work, education, and personal purposes. State officials argue that OpenAI's alleged safety lapses put Florida residents at risk while the company pursued rapid growth and market dominance. The case could set precedent for how states regulate AI companies operating within their borders and establish new standards for disclosure of AI-related risks to consumers.

The lawsuit seeks unspecified damages and injunctive relief to force OpenAI to implement stronger safety measures. Legal experts say the case could take years to resolve and may prompt other states to file similar actions. OpenAI has not yet publicly responded to the specific allegations in Florida's complaint. The outcome will likely influence how AI companies balance innovation with safety considerations and what legal obligations they have to disclose potential dangers to users in Florida and beyond.

cards.teaser: A Florida county has experienced declining property value growth for four consecutive years, a trend that could affect tax revenues and local government budgets.

Recreational boaters in Stuart, Fort Pierce, Vero Beach, and other Treasure Coast communities have reduced their time on the water or shifted to closer inshore locations to minimize fuel consumption. Charter fishing operations face difficult decisions about pricing and trip frequency as diesel and gasoline costs eat into profit margins. Commercial fishermen working out of local marinas see fuel as one of their largest operating expenses, directly affecting the economics of fishing trips.

The Indian River Lagoon and nearshore Atlantic waters remain popular destinations for anglers seeking to avoid long runs that consume excessive fuel. Marina operators and fuel dock attendants report that boaters are more conscious of fuel efficiency and trip planning. The high prices show no immediate signs of declining, meaning Treasure Coast boating enthusiasts will continue adjusting their activities to account for elevated fuel costs throughout the season.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman loses home and photos of late son after lightning strike destroys house
cards.teaser: Rosa Rivera returned from getting a haircut at church last month to find her Fort Pierce home destroyed by fire after a lightning strike, losing irreplaceable photos of her son who died three years ago.
cards.body:
Rosa Rivera, a disabled Fort Pierce woman, is displaced and calling for help after a lightning strike tore through her home last month, leaving her with broken windows, heavy damage, and almost nothing left. When she returned home from getting a haircut at church, a utility worker stopped her outside to tell her the house was on fire. St. Lucie County District Firefighters rushed to put out the flames, and Rivera was told a lightning strike caused the fire.

Walking into her damaged home left Rivera stunned. She lost clothes, furniture and irreplaceable personal belongings including photos of her late son. Rivera's son passed away three years ago, making those photos impossible to replace. The damage left Rivera without insurance and now staying at her nephew's home while she rebuilds. Rivera said she is truly grateful for her nephew because without him, she does not know where she would be.

Rivera, who is disabled, was recovering from neck fusion surgery the same week she lost her home. She described the situation as very overwhelming with a lot to deal with. A memorial outside the damaged home is one of the few things Rivera has left that cannot be replaced. Despite losing nearly everything, Rivera is working to rebuild her life in Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: Jupiter swears in 91 firefighters for town's first-ever fire department at Maltz Jupiter Theatre
cards.teaser: Jupiter made history Monday as 91 firefighters took their oath of service at the Maltz Jupiter Theatre, officially launching Jupiter Fire Rescue as the town's first-ever fire department.
cards.body:
Ninety-one firefighters and their families gathered at the Maltz Jupiter Theatre on Monday as Jupiter officially launched Jupiter Fire Rescue. For Fire Chief Darrel Donatto, the ceremony marked the culmination of more than two years of work building a department from the ground up. Donatto said Monday was the most proud day of his 45-year career in the fire service, getting to swear in 91 new firefighters for the town of Jupiter.

Among the newest members of Jupiter Fire Rescue is Lieutenant Christian Lainhart, a sixth-generation Jupiter resident. After years serving with Martin County Fire Rescue, he saw the chance to serve at home. Lainhart said he is truly blessed and that his roots are his responsibility. He explained that his community developed his character and embedded it into him, and now he is able to deliver that back to the citizens of the community where he was born and raised.

Behind every firefighter is a family making sacrifices. Lainhart's wife, Jessica Lainhart, also grew up in Jupiter and watched her husband become one of the first firefighters in the town's history. She has watched Christian miss many Christmases and Thanksgivings while working. The new Jupiter Fire Rescue department represents a major milestone for the town, establishing local fire protection services for residents.

cards.headline: Loxahatchee residents celebrate completion of new levee 15 years after Tropical Storm Isaac floods
cards.teaser: Nearly fifteen years after Tropical Storm Isaac caused devastating floods in North Loxahatchee, a brand-new levee is finally complete, providing protection for residents who watched the old levee fail in 2012.
cards.body:
A brand-new levee in North Loxahatchee is finally complete, nearly fifteen years after devastating floods wrecked the area during Tropical Storm Isaac. The levee is taller, wider, and safer than the one that failed in 2012, leaving homes underwater, roads impassable, and residents stranded for days. For people in the area, the memory of the flood is not just history but personal.

Argue, with the Indian Trail Improvement District, remembers the uphill battle to secure funding for the critical upgrade. She said funding never got final budget approval because lawmakers did not see the project as a priority. In 2013, the state appropriated $4 million for Phase I, protecting mostly agricultural land, but the eastern portion shielding neighborhoods was left incomplete when funding dried up. It took years of lobbying, partnerships, and persistence from multiple organizations, local and state officials, and residents to finally secure the $10.4 million needed for Phase II, which stretches over 5 miles in total and now completes the levee system.

Everett Mitchell still remembers watching from his front porch as the old levee collapsed during Isaac. Water poured into homes from his home south, trapping neighbors inside. Some escaped on boats and canoes. The new levee provides protection for Loxahatchee residents who lived through the 2012 flooding and feared it could happen again.

cards.headline: Wellington school zone speed cameras issued over 21,000 tickets before shutting off for summer
cards.teaser: Wellington's 11 school zone speed cameras are turned off for summer break after issuing more than 21,000 tickets since September, with state law not covering summer school as a regularly scheduled program.
cards.body:
Wellington installed speed cameras in 11 school zones last fall, but Village Manager Jim Barnes says they will not be active during summer break. The reason is that current state law does not consider summer school a regularly scheduled education program, which is required to trigger enforcement. Barnes explained that summer school at this point does not meet the definition of a regularly scheduled education program, so the cameras will not be active during the summer. However, Barnes hinted that if the cameras stay in place, summer enforcement might eventually happen.

Since the cameras were installed, Wellington residents have had strong opinions on both sides. Some see them as essential for child safety, while others question the village's true motives. Lauren Brody questioned whether the village is trying to keep students and parents safe or trying to give people tickets and generate revenue for the village of Wellington.

Despite the controversy, the cameras have been busy. Since September, they have issued more than 21,000 tickets, with October being the peak month at 5,100 tickets. Barnes says the data proves the cameras work and that Wellington is seeing a considerable amount of speed reduction in school zones. The cameras will remain inactive until the fall when regularly scheduled education programs resume in Wellington schools.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Gardens serves as World Cup training base for Portugal and England at Gardens District Park
cards.teaser: Palm Beach Gardens became a World Cup training base for Portugal and England at Gardens District Park, a facility that has earned a reputation among elite soccer organizations since opening in 2019.
cards.body:
Palm Beach Gardens is serving as a training base for some of the World Cup tournament's biggest teams, including Portugal and England. Gardens District Park, the city's premier soccer facility, was selected as a base camp after years of building a reputation among elite soccer organizations. Sports and Special Facilities Director Tim Ford said that over the last several years, the facility has earned quite a reputation.

Ford said the fields were completed in 2019 and quickly drew national attention. The U.S. Soccer Federation began using the site in 2020 and has since hosted dozens of national youth team training camps. This year, seven Major League Soccer teams used it as a training site. Word spread internationally after Real Madrid used the facility last year. Portugal then selected it as a base camp for this year's World Cup, and England will also stop by to acclimate to the weather as it prepares for some pre-tournament matches in Florida.

Once the last flag football game wrapped up at Gardens District Park in early May, the city's agronomy team got to work preparing the fields for Portugal's arrival. The Director of Agronomy and his team worked to ensure the fields meet the standards expected by international soccer teams. Palm Beach Gardens is now recognized as a premier training destination for elite soccer organizations.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie woman charged with attempted murder, arson after trapping mother in burning bedroom
hero.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman faces charges of attempted murder and arson after allegedly setting fire to a bedroom door while a 62-year-old woman was trapped inside the room Sunday night. Michelle Picard, 26, was arrested following the domestic disturbance and house fire in the 1500 block of Southeast Airoso Boulevard.

Port St. Lucie Police Department officers responded to the scene at around 9:05 p.m. Sunday. The victim first noticed smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door and discovered Picard standing nearby when she opened it. When the victim attempted to retrieve a fire extinguisher, Picard allegedly physically attacked her and tried to prevent her from putting out the fire. Police say Picard made threatening statements and attempted to push the victim toward the flames.

The victim managed to escape to a bathroom, lock the door, and call 911. During the emergency call, Picard could be heard banging on the bathroom door in the background. Officers arrived to find flames inside the residence and immediately worked to evacuate everyone safely.

Officers found Picard outside the residence and detained her. She resisted arrest, causing injuries to one officer's leg and requiring another officer to assist in taking her into custody. The Port St. Lucie Police Department continues to investigate the incident.

cards.headline: North Miami man arrested after attempted armed kidnapping at Port St. Lucie church
cards.teaser: A 64-year-old man armed with a handgun attempted to kidnap a 74-year-old woman in the parking lot of First United Methodist Church on Southwest Prima Vista Boulevard, but witnesses intervened.
cards.body:
Jose Tsu Zamora, 64, of North Miami was arrested Sunday evening after allegedly attempting to kidnap a 74-year-old woman in the parking lot of First United Methodist Church on Southwest Prima Vista Boulevard. The incident unfolded around 10:49 a.m. Sunday morning. Zamora previously had a romantic relationship with the victim and approached her despite an active injunction prohibiting any contact with her.

Port St. Lucie Police Department reports that Zamora, while armed with a handgun, grabbed the victim by her arms and attempted to force her into his vehicle against her will. Several witnesses saw the incident and immediately intervened. Two Good Samaritans confronted Zamora and ordered him to release the victim. During the confrontation, Zamora displayed his firearm before retreating to his vehicle and fleeing the scene.

Church surveillance footage captured portions of the encounter and corroborated witness statements, showing Zamora pursuing the victim. Zamora faces multiple felony charges following his arrest Sunday evening. The Port St. Lucie Police Department continues to investigate the incident. The victim was not physically injured during the attempted kidnapping.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman displaced after lightning strike destroys home, loses photos of late son
cards.teaser: Rosa Rivera returned from church to find her Fort Pierce home on fire after a lightning strike. She lost irreplaceable photos of her son who passed away three years ago and is now staying with her nephew.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce woman is displaced and calling for help after a lightning strike tore through her home last month, leaving her with broken windows, heavy damage, and almost nothing left. Rosa Rivera returned home from getting a haircut at church when a utility worker stopped her outside and told her he thought her house was on fire.

St. Lucie County District Firefighters rushed to put out the flames. Rivera was told a lightning strike caused the fire. Walking into her damaged home left her stunned. Rivera lost clothes, furniture and irreplaceable personal belongings including photos of her late son who passed away three years ago. The damage left Rivera displaced. She is uninsured and is now staying at her nephew's home while she rebuilds.

Rivera, who is also disabled, was recovering from neck fusion surgery the same week she lost her home. A memorial outside the damaged home is one of the few things Rivera has left that cannot be replaced. Rivera said the situation is very overwhelming as she deals with both her recovery and the loss of her home and belongings.

cards.headline: Second victim comes forward against former St. Lucie County school bus driver
cards.teaser: Edwin Garcia, 72, of Port St. Lucie faces an additional battery charge after a second victim came forward with allegations of inappropriate conduct while he was a school bus driver.
cards.body:
A former St. Lucie County school bus driver is facing an additional charge after a second victim came forward in an ongoing investigation into allegations of inappropriate conduct with children. Edwin Garcia, 72, of Port St. Lucie was arrested on a new battery charge May 28 when a second victim came forward with additional information for investigators. This comes after his initial arrest March 6 on two counts of lewd and lascivious molestation of a victim under 12 years of age.

The investigation began March 4 when a school resource deputy received a report that Garcia had allegedly asked a 9-year-old student to lift her dress while riding the school bus. During the preliminary investigation, deputies developed additional information suggesting Garcia may have made inappropriate comments to the child and possibly pinched her over her clothing in the pelvic area, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. The case was then referred to the Criminal Investigations Division, leading to Garcia's initial arrest two days later on March 6.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office continues to investigate the allegations and is encouraging anyone who may have been a victim or has additional information to come forward. Anyone with information related to this case can contact Detective Corporal Hunter Limb at 772-462-7300.
